Summary: Translation is rendering Scripture from Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek into the languages people actually speak - work the church has done since the Septuagint, three centuries before Christ. Every translation involves interpretation, which is why Christians use several and compare them, and why new translations keep appearing as language changes and manuscripts improve. The doctrine beneath it is confidence: God's Word can be faithfully carried across languages, because its Author intends to be understood.
RelatedDoctrines: Inspiration of Scripture; Inerrancy of Scripture
